To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The mh(2J)/AP3d(IAP) mutation is due an insertion of an IAP element in the Ap3D1 gene.

the mh(1J) mutation is caused by an IAP insertion in the Ap-3d gene leading a C-terminually truncated protein, that despite correct assembly of the complex, AP-3 remains impaired in neurons, and that mh(2J)/mh mice show abnormal patterns of zinc staining in the neocortex, but not in the hippocampus, suggesting a cell-specific role for the C-terminus of the delta subunits in AP-3 function.
a mouse mutant with a truncated delta subunit of the AP-1 adaptor complex has a milder phenotype than a mouse mutant that has a deleted delta subunit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic and phenotypic characterization of the mouse mutant Mh2J, an allele caused by Iap element insertion.
the genetic and phenotypic characterization of the mh2J allele.
the molecular mechanisms of the mouse model mh2J, which shows a different phenotype compared to the mh model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mh(1J) and mh(2J)/Ap3d alleles differ in the severity of their neurological phenotypes and in the degree of coat color dilution.
mice mutant for Ap3d have defects in the function of the AP- 3 complex in neurons, and that these defects are responsible for the behavioral abnormalities in mh mice.
the mh(1J) mutation causes a severe reduction in AP-3 complex function in the CNS, while the mh(2) mutation results in a partial reduction in AP-4 complex function in the neocortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mh2J allele is a hypomorphic allele, with a phenotype that varies depending on the cell type.
the delta subunit of AP-3 complex is a key factor for the function of AP-3, and its N-terminal portion is essential for the function of the complex.

the N-terminal part of the delta subunits is sufficient for AP3 complex assembly and localization to the Golgi/endosome, whereas subsequent function is regulated by cell-specific interactions of the C-terminal portion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-terminal portion of the AP- 3 delta subunit plays a critical role in the proper function of the AP- complex.
the mh and mh(2J)/mh(2J) mouse lines are useful tools to investigate the role of AP-3 in neurobiology, and that the mh(1) allele is the most severe of the three alleles, with mh(2J)>mh(2J).
the N-terminal region of delta is sufficient for AP3 complex assembly and localization to the T-G-N, while the C-terminal region is important for the regulation of the complex's function in neurons.
